The React kit is part of `@polaris-key/react`. It runs in a browser page (on Polaris Key's origin,
your own, or in Tauri) and in the Electron renderer. Every catalog component is a React component
over the shared headless layer, and draws the same DOM under the same stylesheet as the web
components kit, so a state looks the same in both. The kit takes its product identity from the
provider configuration. The rest of the SDK is on the [React](/docs/build/sdks/react/) page.

<KitFacts kit="react" />

## Install

From Polaris Key's npm feed ([Installing the SDKs from the feeds](/docs/build/install-from-feeds/)),
with the config `pkey sdk --lang react --write` generates
([quickstart](/docs/build/quickstart/react/)):

```sh
# .npmrc: @polaris-key:registry=https://pkg.plrs.im/npm/polaris-key/
pnpm add @polaris-key/react react react-dom
```

React 18 or later. The kit adds its stylesheet to the page itself, once per document, through
`document.adoptedStyleSheets`: never a `<style>` element, which a strict `style-src` refuses. A
server-rendered app imports the same rules in its root layout so the first paint is styled, and
`fonts.css` for Rubik and the kit's mono face (without it the kit draws in metric-matched system
faces):

```ts
import "@polaris-key/react/styles.css";
import "@polaris-key/react/fonts.css";
```

`@polaris-key/react/kit` is marked `"use client"`. `<PolarisKeyProvider config={polarisKey}>` holds
state, so in a Next.js App Router app the file that renders it starts with `"use client"` too.

## The one-line flow

Layer (a): `<PolarisKeyGate>` inside `<PolarisKeyProvider config={polarisKey}>` starts itself.

```tsx
import { PolarisKeyProvider } from "@polaris-key/react";
import { PolarisKeyGate } from "@polaris-key/react/kit";
import { polarisKey } from "./polaris.config";

export function App() {
  return (
    <PolarisKeyProvider config={polarisKey}>
      <PolarisKeyGate>
        <YourApp />
      </PolarisKeyGate>
    </PolarisKeyProvider>
  );
}
```

The gate never shows sign-in while a cached session is checked. It renders your app once the license
holds, under the grace banner while offline grace runs. Until then it owns the window and runs
Welcome, sign-in with the browser hand-off and its code, Use a license key, the device limit, and
the blocking states with their fixes (Try again, Reconnect, Sign out). A device limit is a neutral
callout whose one primary, Replace a device, opens the license's page with `returnUrl` and the typed
key; the key is tried again when the person comes back. Escape backs out of a step, and focus
follows each new screen. Every control also reaches `onAction`.

## Piecemeal

Layer (b): every catalog component is a React component on `@polaris-key/react/kit`, under its
catalog name. It draws the state its `input` describes (a `UiInput`: what your app knows now) and
reports each control instead of calling the SDK.

| Prop        | What it does                                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`     | The state to draw                                                                                                               |
| `onAction`  | A control was pressed: its copy key (`key`), the shared vocabulary action or `null` (`action`), and the `component` and `state` |
| `onInput`   | The person typed in a field (`key`, `rename`)                                                                                   |
| `onSelect`  | The person picked a row: a device, a license                                                                                    |
| `bare`      | An embedded pane without its own frame                                                                                          |
| `fill`      | A blocking screen that owns the window                                                                                          |
| `autoFocus` | Take focus on mount                                                                                                             |
| `className` | Extra classes on the kit root                                                                                                   |

| Kind   | Components                                                                                                                                               | Layout                                                                        |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Screen | `Boot`, `Welcome`, `SignIn`, `SignInHandoff`, `Activate`, `OfflineActivation`, `DeviceLimit`, `LicenseChoice`, `UpdatePrompt`, `StatusScreen`, `Paywall` | A card on the product's blurred icon; two columns in a short landscape window |
| Pane   | `Devices`, `Settings`, `AccountAndLicense`, `ReleaseNotes`, `About`, `ChannelPicker`                                                                     | From your container's start edge, up to 40rem, framed unless `bare`           |
| Banner | `GraceBanner`                                                                                                                                            | One line, its consequence and at most two actions                             |
| Toast  | `Toast`                                                                                                                                                  | One line, with a visible timer where the state has one                        |
| Inline | `UpdateProgress`, `EntitlementGate`, `CloudSyncStatus`                                                                                                   | A small status inside your layout                                             |

```tsx
import { Devices, type KitAction, type UiInput } from "@polaris-key/react/kit";

export function DevicesSection(props: {
  input: UiInput;
  onAction: (a: KitAction) => void;
}) {
  return <Devices input={props.input} onAction={props.onAction} bare />;
}
```

Restyle with plain CSS. Every component draws in a `.pk-root` element carrying `data-component`,
`data-state`, `data-theme` (`dark` or `light`), `data-preset`, `data-density` and `data-motion`.
Inside it each part has a `data-part` name (`card`, `header`, `icon`, `title`, `lede`, `actions`,
`primary`, `secondary`, `key-field`, `code`, `qr`, `seat-meter`, `device-row`, `license-row`,
`settings-row`, `callout`, `progress`, …) and each control a `data-key`, its copy key. The theme's
colors, radii, type and spacing are `--pk-*` variables on `.pk-root`, never on `:root`. The kit's
rules sit in `@layer polaris-key`, so any rule of yours wins without `!important`:

```css
.pk-root [data-part="primary"] {
  border-radius: 999px;
}
```

## The sign-in form

`SignIn` is the one sign-in form. Its body morphs in place through the steps: the sign-in methods,
the browser hand-off or its code, the license choice and Replace a device, or a license key, then
Done. Nothing stacks on it.

| Prop           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `primitives`   | The SDK's sign-in primitives: the form drives them itself through `SignInModel`. Without them it draws the `input` it is given and reports every control                                      |
| `presentation` | `"inline"` (default) in the page; `"sheet"`, a modal dialog over the page (a bottom sheet on a narrow window) that Escape closes, focus returning to the opener; `"browser"`, the hosted card |
| `replace`      | Where Replace a device runs: `"inline"` or `"browser"`                                                                                                                                        |
| `open`         | The sheet is open                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `onDone`       | The person pressed Start using the product on Done                                                                                                                                            |
| `onClose`      | The sheet closed                                                                                                                                                                              |

The steps morph: the card's height eases from one step's to the next and the new step enters from the
side of travel, through the Web Animations API (no injected styles). Under reduced motion, or
`motion: "none"`, a step swaps at once. Focus moves to the new step's heading.

For a form you lay out yourself, the step parts draw one step each: `SignInMethods`,
`SignInHandoff`, `LicenseChoice`, `ReplaceDevice`, `Activate` and `SignInDone`.
`useSignIn({ primitives, presentation, replace, input })` returns `{ model, input, step }`: the live
`SignInModel` (`null` without primitives), the form's input, and `step.body`, the view the card
draws now.

## Headless

Layer (c): ui-core's models, re-exported from `@polaris-key/react/kit`. `viewOf(component, input)`
returns a component's `View`: its state, the copy keys it shows with their arguments, the actions
its controls perform, and its decisions (the primary control, where focus goes, the link a control
opens). `ViewModel` holds one component's view over a changing input, with the loading delay.
`SignInModel` runs the sign-in form over the SDK's primitives.

```tsx
import { viewOf, type UiInput } from "@polaris-key/react/kit";

export function GateState(props: { input: UiInput }) {
  const view = viewOf("PolarisKeyGate", props.input);
  return <p data-state={view.state}>{view.copy.length} strings</p>;
}
```

The SDK's own hooks (`useLicenseGate()`, `usePolarisAuth()`, `useEntitlement(name)`, …) are on the
[React](/docs/build/sdks/react/) page.

## Styling and presentation

`<PolarisKeyProvider>` holds transport configuration, not styling. Wrap kit components in
`<PolarisKeyTheme theme={…}>` or give an individual component its `theme` prop; an inner theme
layers over an outer one. When a theme leaves them unset, the kit resolves the product name, accent
and verified icon from the adapter's presentation source.

Every kit root has `.pk-root`, `data-part`, `data-key` and `data-state` attributes, while the shared
rules are in the `@layer polaris-key` cascade layer so host CSS wins without `!important`.

The presentation icon is shown as a `blob:` URL, so a page with a Content-Security-Policy allows
`img-src blob:` and `connect-src` for the image origin. With no verified icon, the kit draws a
monogram rather than a Polaris Key mark.

## Localization

Every string is a key of the kit's copy catalog. English is bundled; `de`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `ja`,
`ko`, `pt-BR` and `zh-Hans` load once, on demand, and every component showing that locale redraws
when it arrives. The locale follows the document's `lang`, then the browser's language.

## Removed legacy components

The components of earlier releases that styled themselves inline are removed, with no alias: the
license gate, the login card, the sign-out button, the device manager, the config panel and the
update prompt. Their replacements are on `@polaris-key/react/kit`: `PolarisKeyGate` is the gate and
the login, `Devices` the device list, `Settings` the settings pane, `AccountAndLicense` carries Sign
out, and `UpdatePrompt` draws the update prompt. The `@polaris-key/react/update` subpath stays for
`useLatestVersion` and `useUpdateDecision`; only its prompt is gone. The helper that opened the
device-limit link is removed as well: add `withManageReturn` and `withManageKey` to the refusal's
link and open it yourself, as [Your own UI](/docs/build/sdks/react/your-own-ui/) does.

## Sample

`examples/ui/react-vite/` runs the whole flow in a Vite app, and `examples/ui/react-next/` is a
Next.js App Router app with the `"use client"` boundary and the stylesheet imported in the layout.
Both run against the SDK's fixture adapters with no Worker; each README has the commands, and the
switch to a live Worker.
